claim: Immediate memory is limited by number of chunks, not bits; recoding into larger chunks raises the content held.
agent_test: Store subgoals as named chunks; compare context budget in chunk count vs raw tokens at equal tokens.

claim: Working capacity is nearer 3-5 chunks than 7, and the number depends on how a chunk is defined and on presentation time.
agent_test: Cap the active subgoal set at 4 vs 7 vs 12 items; measure accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Experts recall meaningful positions far better than novices (master about 16 pieces vs 4 in the founding study; 93% vs 33% in the popular summary; replicated with larger N).
agent_test: Compare agent with vs without a domain pattern library on in-distribution tasks at equal tokens.

claim: The skill edge on random material is small but real: r=.41 (CI .29-.51, k=28, N=903), .29 after trim-and-fill; 49 of 55 experiments positive. The founding null on random boards was a 3-player result.
agent_test: Check scaffold gains on shuffled or novel tasks; expect a small residual benefit.

claim: The chunk boundary at about 2 s between placements replicated with a computer display (79.5% of within-glance latencies under 2 s vs 1.1% between glances).
agent_test: Not directly testable on an LLM.

claim: Chunk size is not stable across methods: master largest chunk about 5 pieces (1973) vs 14-17 (computer display) vs 4.6 (repeated-recall method). The measure drives the number.
agent_test: Do not hard-code a chunk size; test three library granularities.

claim: Chunks are location and format specific: mirror reflection hurts recall, more for masters, so chunks do not survive a change of surface form.
agent_test: Retrieve subgoals with paraphrased or reformatted problems; measure the hit-rate drop.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Templates (about 12 fixed items plus slots, 1-2 s slot fill vs 8 s for a new chunk) let experts exceed 7+-2 chunks over several boards; a trained master reached 9 boards via a retrieval structure.
agent_test: Compare fixed-text subgoals vs templates with slots at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval structures extend span by training but stay domain-bound: S.F. digit span 7 to about 79, letter span stayed 7.
agent_test: Build a library on one task family; measure transfer to other families.

claim: The expert memory advantage for domain material appears outside games: fingerprints (d=1.76, N=44+44), bridge (suit grouping), music (r=.69).
agent_test: Not directly testable.

claim: Interference and delay barely hurt chess recall (6-8% drop after 30 s), against a pure short-term chunk store.
agent_test: Not directly testable.

claim: Rival accounts (SEEK, long-term working memory, abstract relations) explain the random-board edge differently; the data do not separate them cleanly.
agent_test: Not directly testable.

claim: LLM chess skill falls with distance from training data: centipawn loss 4.75x worse near and 7.79x worse on random boards; illegal moves 4.72x more on random; base models no better than random legal play on random boards.
agent_test: Rerun on our model: familiar vs perturbed vs random tasks, with and without scaffold.

claim: Extra reasoning tokens help less per token the less familiar the position. GPT-5 (moderate effort) used 3,426 / 11,800 / 16,953 tokens on well-known / near / random positions; relative gain per 1,000 tokens was 22.55% / 7.23% / 3.81% (v3 full text; earlier abstract-level figures differ).
agent_test: Measure gain per 1,000 thinking tokens by task familiarity; allocate thinking by library hit.

claim: Executable skill libraries help LLM agents (Voyager 3.3x items, up to 15.3x faster milestones; library removal plateaus late, qualitative).
agent_test: Ablate the library at equal tokens.

claim: Library-learning gains may not come from reuse: LEGO-Prover reused one lemma once; TroVE had 3 reuses in 3,201 questions; a no-reuse ablation matched or beat TroVE on 3 of 4 splits; self-correction and self-consistency explain gains. Gap search: ReasoningBank and SkillEvolBench still report no zero-reuse ablation; SkillEvolBench shows raw-trace replay often beats distilled skills.
agent_test: Log reuse rate; run a no-reuse ablation before crediting the library.

claim: Retrieved reusable routines or templates raise agent accuracy (AWM +12.0 points on WebArena; BoT Game of 24 82.4% vs ToT 74.0%), but results are paper-reported with differing baselines.
agent_test: Compare template retrieval vs none vs random templates at equal tokens.

claim: Naming and documenting abstractions matters: raw compressed abstractions hurt an LLM (-30.60 REGEX) while documented ones helped (LILO).
agent_test: Test subgoal entries with a description vs code only.

claim: No study gives LLMs the Chase-Simon recall task directly; the nearest is the chess familiarity study, which measures move quality. Gap search 2026-11: only a span-style n-back study (Gong 2023) was found; no chunked-vs-unchunked or shuffled-vs-meaningful recall study.
agent_test: Run our own meaningful-vs-shuffled recall probe.

claim: Unfiltered (add-all) memory or skill libraries do worse than a small verified one; a validation gate and pruning matter most.
agent_test: Arms: add-all vs verified-only vs fixed small library, equal tokens; log delete-by-utility.

claim: A larger active set or bigger library can lower success: retrieving 1 item gave 49.7, 4 gave 44.4 (ReasoningBank); big Tier-3 libraries cut ESR 35.6 to 27.8 (Gemini 3 Flash).
agent_test: Sweep retrieved chunks k=1,2,3,5 at equal tokens.

claim: Distilled skills often lose to replaying raw trajectories, and curated static skills hurt on average (7 of 10 models).
schema_part: memory: keep concrete trace beside abstraction
agent_test: Add a raw-trace arm to the library ablation.

claim: Best skill granularity depends on model and task; no single chunk size wins. Mixed-granularity retrieval beat flat libraries on ALFWorld (51.31 vs 47.14).
agent_test: Store each subgoal at 2 to 3 sizes; let the retriever choose; check on the target model.

claim: Retrieval keyed on task wording alone fails under surface change; adding a structure signal restored reuse (WebArena 39.2 to 45.7, no-skill 38.5).
agent_test: Paraphrase and reorder test on the subgoal library; compare text-only vs state-shape keys.

claim: Thinking-token budget should not follow unfamiliarity upward: models spend more tokens on unfamiliar items but gain less per token; memory makes extra compute pay (no-memory best-of-5 42.2 vs memory single 49.7).
agent_test: Cap tokens per library-miss task; compare with and without a library at the same token total.

claim: Whether slot-filled templates beat fixed chunks for LLM agents has not been tested in a controlled contrast; cross-site slot templates are used (SkillMigrator, PolySkill) but only compared with other systems.
agent_test: Same routines with and without slots, equal tokens.

claim: A skill library moves across models (SkillWeaver: up to +54.3% for weaker agents) but is not shown to move across domains; no replication of Pleiss et al. by an independent team was found (same team added Claude Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3 Flash).
agent_test: Train library in domain A, test in B; report hit rate.

claim: Executable verified skills beat text skills on WebArena (+11.3% relative, ASI), while skill text length needs tuning per model (Qwen3-8B hurt by all skill levels). No cross-task test of named-documented vs code-only chunks was found.
agent_test: Named+documented vs code-only vs text-only on 3 task types.
